# ravyn

Node.js telemetry SDK for the [Ravyn](./docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) ingestion gateway. Captures
**logs, errors, traces, and metrics** and ships them to your project's DSN — without ever crashing
the host app.

- **Zero-config capture.** `console.*`, Pino, Winston, and raw `stdout` are patched automatically.
  Uncaught exceptions and unhandled rejections are reported with structured stack traces.
- **Never throws into your app.** Every host boundary is fault-isolated; an SDK fault degrades the
  SDK, never your process.
- **One pipe for all four signals.** Logs/errors and OTel traces/metrics share one queue, retry
  policy, circuit breaker, and endpoint.
- **Dual ESM + CJS**, typed, with optional `express` / `nestjs` integrations.

## Install

```sh
npm install @ravyn-team/node
```

Framework integrations rely on **peer dependencies** you already have (`express`, `pino`,
`winston`, `@nestjs/*`). Nothing is pulled in unless you use it.

## Usage

Call `init()` **once, before anything else** — see [Load order](#load-order). The DSN is the only
required option.

```js
import { init } from '@ravyn-team/node';

const sdk = init({
  dsn: 'https://<publicKey>@ingest.ravyn.io/<projectId>',
  service: 'my-api',
  environment: 'production',
  release: 'my-api@1.4.2',
});

console.log('hello');           // captured and shipped automatically
sdk.captureException(err);      // report a caught error by hand
await sdk.deliver();            // flush now (optional — auto-flushes on a timer + on shutdown)
```

That's the whole integration: no transports to register, no logger to wrap. CJS is identical with
`const { init } = require('@ravyn-team/node')`.

### API

```ts
init(options): Sdk | undefined    // idempotent; returns undefined when enabled: false
captureException(error): void     // report a caught error
flush(): Promise<void>            // drain the queue now
shutdown(): Promise<void>         // flush + dispose (also runs on SIGTERM/SIGINT)
```

The facade calls are safe no-ops when the SDK is disabled — no `if (sdk)` guards needed.

## Load order

This matters for **traces**. `init()` installs OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation, which can only
patch libraries (`http`, `express`, …) that are loaded **after** it runs. In a native ESM entry
file, `import` statements are hoisted and run before any code in the file body — so this **does not
work**:

```js
import express from 'express';        // ← loaded first, never instrumented
import { init } from '@ravyn-team/node';
init({ dsn: '...' });                  // ← too late; no spans
```

Run the SDK as a preload instead, so it initializes before your app's imports:

```sh
node --import ./instrument.mjs ./dist/index.js
```

```js
// instrument.mjs
import { init } from '@ravyn-team/node';
init({ dsn: '...' });
```

In **CommonJS** this is simpler — just `require` and `init()` before requiring instrumented
libraries:

```js
const { init } = require('@ravyn-team/node');
init({ dsn: '...' });
const express = require('express');    // ← now instrumented
```

Logs, errors, and metrics do **not** need this; only distributed tracing depends on load order.

## Express

```js
import { ExpressIntegration } from '@ravyn-team/node/express';

const ravyn = new ExpressIntegration();
ravyn.setup(sdk);

// ...register routes first...
app.use(ravyn.errorHandler()); // last middleware: reports thrown errors, then re-throws
```

## NestJS

```ts
import { NestIntegration, RavynModule } from '@ravyn-team/node/nestjs';

const ravyn = new NestIntegration();
ravyn.setup(sdk);

@Module({
  imports: [RavynModule.forRoot(ravyn)], // registers the global exception filter
})
export class AppModule {}
```

## Configuration

Invalid config throws at `init()` — the only place the SDK ever throws (setup-time,
developer-facing). Everything except `dsn` has a default.

```ts
init({
  dsn: 'https://<publicKey>@ingest.ravyn.io/<projectId>', // required
  service: 'my-api',          // default "unknown-service"
  environment: 'production',  // default "production"
  release: 'my-api@1.4.2',
  enabled: true,              // false → no-op SDK, nothing patched
  debug: false,               // SDK-internal diagnostics to the original stderr

  tracing: { enabled: true }, // distributed traces (see Load order)
  metrics: {
    enabled: true,            // runtime metrics: event-loop lag, CPU, memory
    intervalMs: 60000,        // export interval
  },
  sampling: {
    traces: 1,                // head-sampling ratio for traces, 0..1
    rate: 1,                  // sampling ratio for logs/errors, 0..1
  },
  transport: { maxBatchSize: 100, flushIntervalMs: 5000, maxQueueSize: 10000 },
  pii: { fields: ['password', 'authorization'], redactDefaults: true },
});
```

Set `tracing.enabled` or `metrics.enabled` to `false` to turn a signal off entirely.
